title: Dam removals are bringing fish back across the northeastern United States
summary: This Smithsonian article reports on the ecological success of dam removal projects across the northeastern United States, where the elimination of small barriers is restoring fish migration routes and revitalizing aquatic ecosystems. Scientists are documenting how native fish species like alewife and American shad are returning to historical habitats after centuries of isolation.
problem_solved: Addresses the ecological problem of fragmented river ecosystems where dams block fish migration and reduce biodiversity.
why_valuable: Demonstrates evidence-based environmental restoration success, showing that strategic dam removal is a cost-effective way to recover native fish populations and river health.
